findings.text: A food truck or cart needs a Mobile Food Facility health permit from DPH, covering plan review of the vehicle, a commissary agreement, and the permit application with initial inspection; the 2026–27 annual license fee for mobile food facilities is $0, and the permit application is $470 with plan review of $414 (low-risk) or $690 (high-risk).

The truck must be permitted by San Francisco DPH even if it holds a health permit from another California county; submit two sets of scaled drawings, interior and exterior photos, a menu, and a commissary agreement through the DPH portal.
findings.verification_note: The record lists commissary agreement as covered but does not state it should be submitted through the DPH portal.

findings.text: A certified food protection manager (one per facility, valid 5 years) is required within 60 days of opening; every employee who handles food must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire.

The DPH mobile food health permit application is sent to the Planning Department for zoning review as an interagency referral, meaning Planning will confirm the mobile food use is permitted before DPH issues the health permit.
findings.verification_note: The record describes the DPH permit process but does not mention Planning Department review or interagency referral.

filing_playbook.action: Request a written Letter of Determination from San Francisco Planning Department confirming whether a mobile food facility is permitted in C-2/Waterfront 2.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the concept is a mobile food truck with limited cooking and no alcohol service, intended to operate in the public right-of-way or on a private lot at or near 430 Beach St in the C-2/Waterfront 2 zoning district. Ask whether mobile vending is a permitted use or requires conditional use authorization or is prohibited under Planning Code §§ 210.1 and 240.2, and whether the Waterfront 2 SUD imposes additional restrictions. Provide a one-page concept description and photos of the vehicle if available. Do not file any location permit or sign a commissary lease until Planning confirms in writing that the use is allowed.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector and obtain a Business Account Number (BAN), and file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk if the doing-business-as name differs from the legal entity name.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register within 30 days of starting business; the fee is tiered by gross receipts ($55 up to $100k for 2026–27). File the FBN statement with the County Clerk in person or by mail, then publish once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a California Seller's Permit from CDTFA and register as an employer with EDD if hiring employees.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online at cdtfa.ca.gov for the seller's permit (free, usually issued the same day); it is required for selling food and drinks. If hiring employees, register with EDD e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying more than $100 in wages; free, takes 1–7 days. Set up workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund before the first employee starts.

filing_playbook.action: Submit the mobile food facility health permit application to San Francisco DPH, with vehicle drawings, photos, menu, and a commissary agreement.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply through the DPH portal with two sets of scaled drawings of the truck interior, exterior and interior photos, a menu describing food prep steps, and a commissary agreement. The 2026–27 fees are $470 application plus $414 (low-risk) or $690 (high-risk) plan review.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

timeline_cost.notes: The day range (90–270 days) is the time to obtain the mobile food facility health permit and one Public Works location permit when both are granted, not a time to a denial or withdrawal. The health permit takes 30–90 days (catalog entry sf.mobile_food_facility_health_permit); the location permit takes 60–180 days including posting, neighbor notification, the 30-day comment period, and final issuance (catalog entry sf.mobile_food_facility_location_permit). These run sequentially because the location permit requires the health permit as a prerequisite, so the total is 90–270 days. The cost range ($2,600–$8,500) covers government fees only: entity formation ($70–$150, catalog ca.sos_entity_registration), business registration ($55–$700, sf.business_registration), FBN filing ($60–$120, sf.fictitious_business_name), food safety manager cert ($100–$250, ca.food_safety_manager_cert), mobile health permit ($880–$1,500, sf.mobile_food_facility_health_permit), and one location permit ($1,151–$5,000, sf.mobile_food_facility_location_permit). Each additional location adds $1,151–$5,000 and 60–180 days. These figures assume Planning confirms mobile food vending is permitted in C-2/Waterfront 2; if it is not, or if the concept must be changed to fit within a permitted use, no cost or timeline can be given until the zoning answer is known. The stall risk is high: the catalog warns location permits are routinely appealed by nearby restaurants, and the Fisherman's Wharf tourist corridor has 20 registered food businesses and 11 ABC licenses within 500 ft, so neighbor opposition and appeals are likely to push timelines to the upper end or beyond.
timeline_cost.verification_note: The cited records' fees total $2,316–$7,720, not $2,600–$8,500. Other facts (number of nearby businesses, Planning confirmation, predictions about appeals) are also not in the records.

status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.

records_summary: 430 Beach St is in the C-2 (Community Business) zoning district within the Waterfront 2 Special Use District and the Priority Equity Geographies SUD on the Fisherman's Wharf tourist corridor. The site has operated as a limited restaurant and tea shop since at least 2018, with three health department referrals approved between 2018-01-29 and 2018-04-17. The immediate area is saturated with food businesses: 20 registered food or drink establishments and 11 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft (27 licenses within 1,000 ft), triggering the undue-concentration flag. Mobile food facilities are not covered by the Planning Code rule table, so the pathway analysis shows no use control was looked up and no change-of-use determination was made. The base rate shows zero dated use decisions for comparable businesses within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years (193 records were excluded as building work or agency referrals, and 30 were grant-only permits/licenses), so no approval rate can be calculated.
data_gaps: No Planning Code use control on file for mobile food facilities, so whether a food truck is permitted by right, conditional, or prohibited in C-2/Waterfront 2 is not established by the rule table.
No dated Planning use decisions for mobile food vendors within 1,000 ft in the records period, so no precedent approval rate or timeline data is available.
Waterfront 2 SUD rules as they stood on 2022-04-14 are not exposed in the overlay summary, so specific design or operational constraints are unknown.
No Public Works mobile food facility location permits appear in the Planning records, so the neighborhood reception to food trucks at this address or block is not shown.
ABC license conditions for the 11 nearby on-sale licenses are not extracted, so whether hours, entertainment, or outdoor service restrictions apply nearby is unknown.
